literal: Another's fault he who speaks, his own faults even among, the most hurtful kind having selected, to be spoken will be.
translation: He who speaks of another's faults will have his own faults searched out and spoken of, especially those that are most hurtful.
modern: பிறருடைய குற்றங்களைப் பற்றிப் புறங்கூறிப் பேசுபவனுடைய சொந்தக் குற்றங்களுக்குள்ளும் மிகக் கொடிய குற்றங்களைத் தேடித் தேர்ந்தெடுத்துப் பிறரால் பேசப்படும்.
explanation: This couplet warns against the consequences of backbiting and exposing the flaws of others. If a person gossips about another's faults, society will retaliate by exposing their own flaws. Crucially, people will not just speak of any minor flaw; they will search out and select (தெரிந்து) the most sensitive, hurtful, and damaging secrets (திறன்) to expose. Thus, speaking ill of others ultimately invites the most painful exposure of one's own character.
